pathway.title: Vornado Realty Lp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The New York office franchise is the strongest support and is improving: occupancy rose to 93.0% at 2026-09-30 from 91.2% at 2025-12-31, third-quarter second-generation space was leased 37.2% above prior straight-line rent and 25.9% above prior cash rent, and same-store NOI at share grew 8.4% over nine months. Rent growth on a high occupancy base in the market that supplies 88% of NOI at share lifts the cash available for debt service without new capital. The limit is cash conversion: same-store cash NOI grew only 1.6% because free rent delays cash, and tenant improvements and leasing commissions took 12.0% of initial rent in the quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 57–58, 67, 69; calculation CALC-25; calculation CALC-31

Leverage is high and the FY2025 figure of 4.07x is misleading: trailing total debt is 8.08x EBITDA, or 8.47x excluding printed gains, and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.89x, or 2.76x excluding gains. The FY2025 dip came from a USD 803.25 million lease gain, and the estimated net gain of about USD 485.00 million from the Park Avenue development venture, due in the fourth quarter of 2026, will lift the next trailing EBITDA in the same way and should not be read as deleveraging. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

Look-through leverage is higher than the consolidated ratios, and this module corrects two earlier statements: Financial foundation and Business & governance say no source totals the debt of unconsolidated joint ventures, but the market-risk table in each of the five filings prints the partnership's pro rata share, USD 2,732.55 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 2,478.54 million at 2025-12-31. Added to consolidated principal of USD 7,487.54 million it gives USD 10,220.09 million, or 8.88x NOI at share over the last twelve months against 8.72x at 2025-12-31; after general and administrative costs of USD 156.10 million the ratio is 10.28x. These ratios overstate attributable debt because consolidated debt counts minority-owned joint ventures at 100%, an amount the filings do not state. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 65, 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 87; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-12

Cash generation does not fund the capital programme, so the gap is bridged by borrowing, asset sales and liquidity. In the twelve months to 2026-09-30 operating cash flow of USD 409.27 million exceeded additions to real estate and development spending of USD 357.91 million by only USD 51.36 million; preferred distributions of USD 62.10 million turned that into a shortfall of USD 10.74 million, and the common distribution of USD 141.28 million paid to the trust in the fourth quarter of 2025 widens it to USD 152.02 million. In nine months of 2026 the partnership also put USD 297.12 million into joint ventures, USD 170.32 million into acquisitions and USD 133.40 million of cash into repurchases of units owned by the trust, funded by net borrowings of USD 299.21 million and cash on hand. A further common distribution of about USD 153.30 million would fall due in the fourth quarter if the 2025 dividend rate is repeated. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14

Liquidity is adequate and unsecured maturities are distant, so the pressure point is secured refinancing in 2027 and 2028. Unrestricted cash of USD 580.50 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,188.28 million gives USD 1,768.78 million, 4.30 times the USD 411.03 million of calls identified for the next twelve months (the rest of the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment, the common distribution if repeated and preferred distributions); pro forma net debt after the 2026-10-20 joint venture closing is not established. No unsecured debt matures before April 2029 if as-of-right extensions are used, but mortgages of USD 880.00 million fall due in 2027 and USD 2,300.00 million in 2028; after the USD 400.00 million loan on the Park Avenue development site was satisfied at closing the total is USD 2,780.00 million, besides the USD 244.54 million Seventh Avenue loan in default, whose waiver of default interest runs through March 2027. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 45, 70, 73, 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 128–129; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-17

Unsecured creditors sit behind property-level lenders in practice: mortgages are 65.04% of consolidated principal, the properties pledged carried about USD 6,000.00 million at book at 2025-12-31 against USD 4,944.04 million of mortgages, and the annual report says subsidiary creditors are paid before the partnership receives distributions. About USD 4,155.48 million of real estate at book value was therefore unencumbered against USD 2,270.42 million of unsecured debt, 1.83x at book rather than market values; the legal rank and guarantors of each instrument are not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 101, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-18

Capital allocation favours shareholders and joint ventures over deleveraging, though no extraction is documented: the trust repurchased USD 133.31 million of shares at an average USD 29.41 in nine months (the cash flow statement shows USD 133.40 million) while consolidated borrowings rose, and the largest development depends on one founder's affiliates as lender, 60% partner and anchor tenant. Against that, related-party fees are small, reporting is audited and reviewed, repurchases paused in the third quarter and no priming or non-pro-rata transaction is documented, so financial policy is average rather than weak. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 57, 73

The weaker assets cap upside but do not threaten debt service on their own: street retail occupancy was 78.4% with second-generation cash rents 15.7% lower in the third quarter, THE MART occupancy fell to 79.5%, and same-store cash NOI at the San Francisco office complex fell 42.5% over nine months on free rent. Street retail supplied 16.94% and the Other segment 14.54% of nine-month NOI at share, so the New York office portfolio carries the credit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 57–58, 65, 69; calculation CALC-27

Interest cost is rising and most of the hedge book rolls off in 2027, so interest cover will not improve without EBITDA growth: the weighted average rate on consolidated debt rose to 4.91% from 4.73% at 2025-12-31, the weighted average rate on unsecured notes rose to 4.78% from 2.73% after 5.75% notes due 2033 replaced 2.15% notes, and 26.34% of principal floats. A one percentage point rise in base rates costs USD 11.48 million a year after current hedges, but the swaps and caps on the revolver, the term loan and five mortgage loans expire between February 2027 and October 2027, when the sensitivity will rise by an amount the filings do not state. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 79–81; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 128; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20

The primary downside path is a squeeze in 2027 and 2028, when weaker office leasing or higher base rates would hit cash flow that already barely covers capital spending and preferred distributions just as USD 2,780.00 million of mortgages mature and the partnership begins funding about USD 290.00 million of cash to the Park Avenue development venture in mid-2028. An illustrative reversal of New York office occupancy to the 88.8% of 2024-12-31 would remove about USD 64.85 million of annual rent, lifting trailing leverage excluding gains to 9.15x and cutting cover to 2.47x with a one percentage point rise in base rates; liquidity, unused repurchase authority and asset sales would absorb it, so distress is not the base case. The signals to watch are look-through leverage, New York office occupancy and progress on refinancing the 2027 and 2028 mortgages. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 73, 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-24

runs.text: The credit's strengths are an office franchise that is leasing at higher rents on rising occupancy, a tenant base with no tenant above 10% of revenues and ten largest tenants at 26.9% of rent, an unsecured maturity profile with nothing due before April 2029 if extensions are used, and asset values that appear to sit above book. Each links to cash flow or recovery: higher rents raise NOI, a diversified rent roll limits single-tenant loss, distant unsecured maturities remove a near-term refinancing event for the partnership's bank and note investors, and values above book support sales that repay debt. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 26–27, 45, 57–58; calculation CALC-21; calculation CALC-22

The credit's weaknesses are leverage above eight times on every gross-debt measure, free cash flow that is roughly zero after capital spending and preferred distributions and negative after the common distribution, a secured maturity wall in 2027 and 2028, floating-rate exposure with hedges expiring in 2027, and a large development whose financing, equity and anchor rent depend on one relationship. Each links to the capacity to deleverage: leverage cannot fall from internal cash, refinancing sets the pace, and an equity call beginning in mid-2028 competes with maturities in the same year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 70–73, 79–81; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-17

On the nine financial-profile dimensions the assessment is: scale and market position strong, with trailing revenues of USD 1,842.71 million and 26.50 million square feet in service at the partnership's share; competitive advantage average, strong in New York office and weaker in retail and non-New York assets; business diversification average, with tenant diversification strong and geographic and property-type concentration weak; cost and capex flexibility average; margin stability average; free cash flow stability weak; ability to refinance and access capital markets average; liquidity position strong over twelve months; and financial policy and governance average. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 65, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 52; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-33

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2026 financing steps changed the debt stack. In January the partnership refinanced one revolving credit facility to USD 1,130.00 million and upsized the other to USD 1,000.00 million, and upsized the term loan to USD 850.00 million; it sold USD 500.00 million of 5.75% senior unsecured notes due in 2033 and repaid USD 400.00 million of 2.15% notes at maturity in June; and in February it refinanced USD 525.00 million on One Park Avenue to 2031 at a wider spread. These moves push the bank facilities to 2029 and 2031, the term loan to 2031 and the new notes to 2033, at a higher coupon than the notes repaid. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 56

The new debt that matters most is off the consolidated balance sheet: the USD 575.00 million fixed-rate loan on Park Avenue Plaza, the USD 3,300.00 million construction loan of the 350 Park Avenue joint venture and a USD 48.00 million joint-venture mortgage in default, none of which enters consolidated debt but each of which sits behind equity the partnership has committed or invested. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23, 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt over EBITDA was 9.36x at 2024-12-31, 4.07x at 2025-12-31 and 8.08x on a trailing basis at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA over cash interest was 2.73x, 5.64x and 2.89x. The FY2025 dip is not operating: it comes from USD 838.54 million of printed gains, chiefly the USD 803.25 million lease gain, which sits in both FY2025 and nine-month 2025 EBITDA and cancels out of the trailing figure. Excluding printed gains, total debt was 9.53x EBITDA in FY2024, 7.74x in FY2025 and 8.47x trailing, so underlying leverage improved in 2025 and has since risen again; cover on the same basis was 2.68x, 2.96x and 2.76x. Equity-method income stays inside derived EBITDA and was USD 99.34 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, including a USD 44.33 million gain on sale, against distributions of income from those entities of USD 86.02 million, so cash cover is weaker than the ratios imply. The consequence for creditors is debt of roughly eight times trailing EBITDA with cover under three times and floating-rate mortgages at a weighted average of 5.65% against 4.98% on fixed-rate mortgages, which leaves little room for lower rents or higher refinancing costs.

fields.value: Net debt rose by USD 523.04 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Investing outflows of USD 600.54 million, led by USD 297.12 million into partially owned entities, USD 185.55 million of additions to real estate and USD 170.32 million of acquisitions, and USD 133.40 million of Class A unit repurchases were funded by operating cash flow of USD 263.00 million and net borrowings of USD 299.21 million, while cash fell by USD 260.35 million. Operating cash flow is a weaker guide than it looks: the nine months to 2025 included USD 901.41 million of prepaid lease payment from a tenant, which more than explains the fall from USD 1,112.11 million to USD 263.00 million. On a trailing basis operating cash flow of USD 409.27 million, already after cash interest of USD 318.80 million, exceeded additions to real estate and development spending of USD 357.91 million by only USD 51.36 million, and USD 62.10 million of preferred distributions left cash flow about USD 10.74 million short.

fields.value: Several choices change the numbers and are logged in the definition register. Debt is carrying value of USD 7,448.31 million at 2026-09-30, USD 39.23 million below contractual principal of USD 7,487.54 million; lease liabilities of USD 694.36 million sit on their own line and are not debt; cash excludes restricted cash; and EBITDA is derived because the issuer prints none. The balance sheet shows no separate customer-deposit, deferred-revenue or supplier-finance line, and the largest non-debt liabilities are lease liabilities and accounts payable and accrued expenses. The trust's funds from operations, which the management discussion also reports, are not partnership figures and appear only as context.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet are excluded from every period figure. The first, on 2026-10-20, formed a joint venture for a Park Avenue office development site, satisfied the USD 400.00 million mortgage loan on the property and deconsolidated it, with an estimated net gain of about USD 485.00 million due in the fourth quarter of 2026; the source gives no cash effect, so pro forma net debt is not established. The second, on 2026-10-26, was a maturity default on a USD 48.00 million non-recourse loan of an unconsolidated joint venture, which does not enter consolidated debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One lease transaction with a major tenant carries three figures with different roles: USD 935.00 million of cash received, USD 901.41 million after initial direct costs in the cash flow statement, and a USD 803.25 million gain in the income statement. Cash analysis uses the cash flow figure and EBITDA analysis the gain, which is why FY2025 and nine-month 2025 differ so sharply from the trailing figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading trailing leverage near eight times as stress is that book debt is 0.48x total assets, that the partnership holds USD 2,244.17 million of investments in partially owned entities whose own debt sits outside consolidated debt while their income sits inside EBITDA, and that management states that cash flow over the next twelve months together with cash on hand will be adequate to fund its needs. What would change the view is a rise in trailing EBITDA from new leasing, or evidence that the unconsolidated joint-venture debt, which no source totals, is large.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is not printed anywhere in the five sources, so EBITDA (Reported) in every period is derived from net income, interest and debt expense, income tax expense and depreciation and amortization; it includes non-operating items and every leverage and cover ratio depends on it, so this is a high-severity gap that only an issuer-stated EBITDA definition would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - FY2025 and nine-month 2025 EBITDA include an USD 803,248 thousand gain on a sales-type lease and other printed gain lines (net gains on disposition of USD 35,291 thousand in FY2025 and USD 24,039 thousand in nine months 2025, and a gain on debt extinguishment of USD 32,073 thousand in nine months 2026); the normalised figures are an Analyst Judgement that removes only those lines, this is a high-severity gap for FY2025 comparisons, and equity-method gains on sale of USD 76,162 thousand in FY2025 and nine months 2025 and USD 44,329 thousand in nine months 2026 remain inside EBITDA because the statements do not print them as separate lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31 and pre-dates the January 2026 refinancing of both revolving facilities and the term loan, the 2033 notes offering and the repayment of the 2026 notes, so the wall at 2026-09-30 cannot be shown; this is a high-severity gap that a ladder at 2026-09-30 would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Two mortgage loans were in maturity default at 2025-12-31: the loan on the Seventh Avenue office building of USD 244,543 thousand, covered by a forbearance agreement signed on 2026-03-09 that waives default interest through March 2027 but is not supplied, and the Broadway loan of USD 74,494 thousand, which was extinguished in May 2026; the forbearance terms cannot be assessed, a medium-severity gap that the agreement itself would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states the legal rank of any debt instrument, so the debt stack has no rows, the Ranking cells in the instrument table are not supplied, and the indentures and credit agreements named in the exhibit list are not supplied; this is a medium-severity gap for any recovery or priority analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No covenant level is stated and covenant compliance is stated only as at year-end in the annual reports, so no covenant headroom is shown and none is inferred; this is a medium-severity gap that the credit agreements would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt of unconsolidated joint ventures is outside consolidated debt while their income is inside EBITDA, and no source totals it; this is a medium-severity gap for leverage on a look-through basis that a schedule of joint-venture debt would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma net debt for the joint venture closing of 2026-10-20 is not established: the source says the USD 400,000 thousand mortgage loan was satisfied at closing and an estimated net gain of about USD 485,000 thousand will be recognised in the fourth quarter of 2026, but not the cash paid or received; this is a medium-severity gap that the next quarterly report would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A mortgage loan of USD 48,000 thousand of an unconsolidated joint venture matured unpaid on 2026-10-26; it is outside consolidated debt and the partnership's share of the joint venture's debt is not totalled, so the consequence for the partnership is not established; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Several lines are printed as dashes and are therefore not supplied rather than zero: in the income statements the gain on debt extinguishment, gain on sales-type lease and net gains on disposition in the periods where they print a dash, in the cash flow statements the prepaid lease payment, gain on sales-type lease, acquisitions of real estate, distributions of capital from partially owned entities, loan receivable, preferred equity redemption, condominium sales and Class A unit repurchase lines in the periods where they print a dash, and net investment in lease at 2024-12-31; this is a low-severity gap that confirmation that a dash means nil would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Some lines exist in one statement but are not printed in another, for example the gain on debt extinguishment in the annual income statements and distributions to Vornado in the nine-month cash flow statements, so those cells are not supplied for the periods that do not print them; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow statements are printed for year-to-date periods only, so there is no third-quarter cash flow column, and the first-quarter and second-quarter income statement columns are not tabulated because the nine-month columns carry the same periods; this is a low-severity gap, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is derived as the year less nine months and labelled calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, so principal is shown by instrument with one financing-cost adjustment of USD -39,231 thousand; the split of the USD 918,000 thousand drawn between the two revolving facilities, the coupon and month of maturity of the 2031 notes, scheduled amortisation and floors are not stated; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Undrawn committed facilities are computed from stated commitments, drawings and letters of credit because the filings print only a rounded total; the computed figures agree with management's rounded statements at all three dates, a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Funds from operations are reported for the trust's common shareholders only and the partnership prints no equivalent, so the dashboard shows them as a trust measure; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment disclosures were recast in the first quarter of 2026, so segment revenue is shown on two property compositions that are never spliced: the 2026 composition for nine months and the third quarter of 2025 and 2026, and the pre-2026 composition for FY2024 and FY2025, with the other composition not supplied in each case; the Other column contains an elimination of cleaning fees that the statements do not print as a separate Corporate and eliminations row; segment revenue reconciles to reported revenue within each basis, a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, so the adjusted EBITDA bridge has no amounts and the optional adjusted EBITDA row is not written; this is a low-severity gap that closes only if the company publishes an adjusted figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Restricted cash of USD 143,339 thousand at 2026-09-30 is excluded from cash; counting it would lower net debt by that amount, a low-severity matter of definition rather than evidence, and cash interest paid includes interest rate cap premiums and excludes capitalized interest.

fields.value: Business and governance facts for Vornado Realty Lp (the operating partnership Vornado Realty L.P.), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business, ownership, operating model, transactions, events and governance from the five supplied filings. This module draws no recovery conclusion and no instrument recommendation.

fields.value: Upstream module output used: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 8a149f3cc3784477f6f9b978e7acf147daa97d0bdc355800d687477693126868. The run settings were read for the periods and are not issuer evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vornado Realty L.P. is a Manhattan-weighted office landlord with diversified tenants and rising occupancy, but acquisitions, joint ventures, development and buybacks under concentrated insider influence make its governance and capital-allocation risk medium for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New York earns 81.93% of revenue and its occupancy rose to 91.5% from 90.0% over nine months; no tenant exceeds 10% of revenue and the ten largest are 26.9% of rent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital is committed ahead of income: USD 230.00 million for a 49.0% stake in Park Avenue Plaza, USD 133.31 million of repurchases in nine months, and a USD 6,250.00 million development whose lender, partner and anchor tenant trace to one founder, with the partnership's cash contribution of about USD 290.00 million starting in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors lend to the operating company itself: the trust is its sole general partner and owns about 91.2% of common units, third-party unitholders hold the rest, and the partnership is the borrower under the bank facilities, so the trust's own claim sits behind the partnership's creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The portfolio is concentrated by market but not by tenant: New York produced 81.93% of revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, no tenant is above 10% of revenues and the largest is 4.5% of rent. Office occupancy rose to 93.0% and second-generation New York office space was signed 37.2% above prior straight-line rent in the third quarter, but street retail occupancy is 78.4% and THE MART fell to 79.5%, so the Other segment is the weaker part of the operating model.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is being funded ahead of cash flow. The partnership paid about USD 230.00 million for a 49.0% stake in Park Avenue Plaza, USD 141.00 million for a redevelopment site, and has spent USD 254.27 million of USD 450.00 million on the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment due for delivery in 2027; the larger commitment is a USD 6,250.00 million joint-venture development in which its share is a USD 500.00 million net contribution of the site and about USD 290.00 million of cash from mid-2028, which competes with debt service and maturities in that year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One founder's affiliates are lender, joint-venture partner and anchor tenant on the largest project: an affiliate lent USD 400.00 million at 4.00% in March 2026, owns 60% of the new venture and the founder's company is the anchor tenant, while the founder's company is also the third-largest tenant at 3.4% of rent, so the project concentrates financing, equity and rent in one relationship.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated but extraction is not documented. The chairman and chief executive of the trust also leads Alexander's, and Interstate Properties and its partners held about 7.1% of the trust's shares and 26.0% of Alexander's, which the annual report says gives them substantial influence; against that, related-party management fees are small (USD 0.20 million from Interstate and USD 5.72 million from Alexander's in FY2025), reporting is audited and no uptier, priming or non-pro-rata transaction is documented. Governance risk is therefore medium, driven by influence and capital allocation rather than by documented creditor-adverse conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions are modest against liquidity but real: the trust repurchased USD 133.31 million of shares in nine months to 2026-09-30 at an average of USD 29.41, authorised a further USD 300.00 million in April 2026, and pays one common dividend a year in the fourth quarter. The program can be paused, none was bought in the third quarter, and nothing in the sources links the buybacks to borrowing, so this is a mild negative for debt reduction rather than extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vno-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distress is confined to non-recourse assets so far. The USD 244.54 million loan on the Seventh Avenue office building matured unpaid in December 2025 and is under a forbearance agreement that waives default interest through March 2027, and a Broadway loan was extinguished through a sale in May 2026 with a USD 32.07 million gain; no recourse to the partnership is stated, but a joint-venture loan of USD 48.00 million also matured unpaid in October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk rating is that the insider group holds only about 7.1% of the trust's shares, related-party management fees are small, reporting is audited and reviewed, repurchases are small against liquidity and paused in the third quarter, defaults were on non-recourse loans, and a partner funds early equity on the largest development. What would change the view is a debt-funded buyback or distribution, a related-party transaction on non-market terms, an amendment or exchange that weakens unsecured creditors, recourse guarantees in the Park Avenue development joint venture agreement, or a lower-than-expected share of joint-venture partners' funding; any of these would move the rating to high, while an end to repurchases and disclosure of the joint-venture terms would move it toward low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, executive pay and the approval of related-party agreements are not assessed; this limits the medium governance rating, which rests on disclosed ownership, fees and reporting only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements, indentures and forbearance agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments and asset transfers is not assessed and willingness is judged only from documented actions; this caps confidence in the capital-allocation view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt of unconsolidated joint ventures is not totalled in any source, so the view that development and joint-venture risk is moderate rests on consolidated figures and could be understated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The joint venture agreement for the Park Avenue development is not supplied, so the partnership's equity commitment beyond mid-2028 and any guarantees are not established; recourse terms would raise the capital-allocation risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No report after the third-quarter filing signed on 2026-11-02 is supplied, so later transactions or defaults would not be seen and the events timeline ends there.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 financing steps changed the debt stack. In January the partnership refinanced one revolving credit facility to USD 1,130.00 million and upsized the other to USD 1,000.00 million, and upsized the term loan to USD 850.00 million; it sold USD 500.00 million of 5.75% senior unsecured notes due in 2033 and repaid USD 400.00 million of 2.15% notes at maturity in June; and in February it refinanced USD 525.00 million on One Park Avenue to 2031 at a wider spread. These moves push the bank facilities to 2029 and 2031, the term loan to 2031 and the new notes to 2033, at a higher coupon than the notes repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt that matters most is off the consolidated balance sheet: the USD 575.00 million fixed-rate loan on Park Avenue Plaza, the USD 3,300.00 million construction loan of the 350 Park Avenue joint venture and a USD 48.00 million joint-venture mortgage in default, none of which enters consolidated debt but each of which sits behind equity the partnership has committed or invested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated insider influence and capital allocation toward joint ventures, development and repurchases, because that competes with debt reduction, which implies a modestly higher probability of weaker creditor outcomes if leverage rises; countervailing evidence is the absence of any documented extraction, small related-party fees, audited reporting and non-recourse defaults, and further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreements and the 350 Park Avenue joint venture agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting is not supplied, so board independence, executive pay and approval of related-party agreements are not assessed; this is a medium-severity gap that the proxy statement would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreements, indentures and forbearance agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments and asset transfers cannot be separated from willingness; this is a medium-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt of unconsolidated joint ventures is not totalled in any source, so look-through leverage is not measured; this is a medium-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 350 Park Avenue joint venture agreement, equity call schedule and any guarantees are not supplied; this is a medium-severity gap for the partnership's funding commitment after mid-2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment revenue is shown on two property compositions that are never spliced, because properties moved to the Other segment in the first quarter of 2026; this is a low-severity gap for revenue mix comparisons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No report after the third-quarter filing signed on 2026-11-02 is supplied, so events in the sixteen days to the as-of date are not covered; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The identity of the 30% owner of 555 California Street and the amount of the 2026 common dividend are not stated; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Vornado Realty Lp (the operating partnership Vornado Realty L.P.), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the partnership's business quality, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring signals from the five supplied filings and the earlier module outputs. It draws no rating, legal-capacity, recovery, relative-value or sizing conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vornado Realty L.P. is an average credit: a Manhattan office franchise with rising rents and USD 1,768.78 million of liquidity offsets leverage of 8.08x EBITDA and cash flow that does not fund its capital programme, so creditors depend on asset cover and refinancing access.

fields.value: Counting USD 2,732.55 million of joint-venture debt that sits outside consolidated debt, leverage is 8.88x NOI at share, and USD 2,780.00 million of mortgages mature in 2027 and 2028. Trailing leverage excluding gains falling below the FY2025 level of 7.74x through earnings growth would strengthen the view; refinancing those mortgages at higher cost without paydown would weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The New York office franchise is the strongest support and is improving: occupancy rose to 93.0% at 2026-09-30 from 91.2% at 2025-12-31, third-quarter second-generation space was leased 37.2% above prior straight-line rent and 25.9% above prior cash rent, and same-store NOI at share grew 8.4% over nine months. Rent growth on a high occupancy base in the market that supplies 88% of NOI at share lifts the cash available for debt service without new capital. The limit is cash conversion: same-store cash NOI grew only 1.6% because free rent delays cash, and tenant improvements and leasing commissions took 12.0% of initial rent in the quarter.

fields.value: Leverage is high and the FY2025 figure of 4.07x is misleading: trailing total debt is 8.08x EBITDA, or 8.47x excluding printed gains, and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.89x, or 2.76x excluding gains. The FY2025 dip came from a USD 803.25 million lease gain, and the estimated net gain of about USD 485.00 million from the Park Avenue development venture, due in the fourth quarter of 2026, will lift the next trailing EBITDA in the same way and should not be read as deleveraging.

fields.value: Look-through leverage is higher than the consolidated ratios, and this module corrects two earlier statements: Financial foundation and Business & governance say no source totals the debt of unconsolidated joint ventures, but the market-risk table in each of the five filings prints the partnership's pro rata share, USD 2,732.55 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 2,478.54 million at 2025-12-31. Added to consolidated principal of USD 7,487.54 million it gives USD 10,220.09 million, or 8.88x NOI at share over the last twelve months against 8.72x at 2025-12-31; after general and administrative costs of USD 156.10 million the ratio is 10.28x. These ratios overstate attributable debt because consolidated debt counts minority-owned joint ventures at 100%, an amount the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not fund the capital programme, so the gap is bridged by borrowing, asset sales and liquidity. In the twelve months to 2026-09-30 operating cash flow of USD 409.27 million exceeded additions to real estate and development spending of USD 357.91 million by only USD 51.36 million; preferred distributions of USD 62.10 million turned that into a shortfall of USD 10.74 million, and the common distribution of USD 141.28 million paid to the trust in the fourth quarter of 2025 widens it to USD 152.02 million. In nine months of 2026 the partnership also put USD 297.12 million into joint ventures, USD 170.32 million into acquisitions and USD 133.40 million of cash into repurchases of units owned by the trust, funded by net borrowings of USD 299.21 million and cash on hand. A further common distribution of about USD 153.30 million would fall due in the fourth quarter if the 2025 dividend rate is repeated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and unsecured maturities are distant, so the pressure point is secured refinancing in 2027 and 2028. Unrestricted cash of USD 580.50 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,188.28 million gives USD 1,768.78 million, 4.30 times the USD 411.03 million of calls identified for the next twelve months (the rest of the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment, the common distribution if repeated and preferred distributions); pro forma net debt after the 2026-10-20 joint venture closing is not established. No unsecured debt matures before April 2029 if as-of-right extensions are used, but mortgages of USD 880.00 million fall due in 2027 and USD 2,300.00 million in 2028; after the USD 400.00 million loan on the Park Avenue development site was satisfied at closing the total is USD 2,780.00 million, besides the USD 244.54 million Seventh Avenue loan in default, whose waiver of default interest runs through March 2027.

fields.value: Unsecured creditors sit behind property-level lenders in practice: mortgages are 65.04% of consolidated principal, the properties pledged carried about USD 6,000.00 million at book at 2025-12-31 against USD 4,944.04 million of mortgages, and the annual report says subsidiary creditors are paid before the partnership receives distributions. About USD 4,155.48 million of real estate at book value was therefore unencumbered against USD 2,270.42 million of unsecured debt, 1.83x at book rather than market values; the legal rank and guarantors of each instrument are not established.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 101, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation favours shareholders and joint ventures over deleveraging, though no extraction is documented: the trust repurchased USD 133.31 million of shares at an average USD 29.41 in nine months (the cash flow statement shows USD 133.40 million) while consolidated borrowings rose, and the largest development depends on one founder's affiliates as lender, 60% partner and anchor tenant. Against that, related-party fees are small, reporting is audited and reviewed, repurchases paused in the third quarter and no priming or non-pro-rata transaction is documented, so financial policy is average rather than weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaker assets cap upside but do not threaten debt service on their own: street retail occupancy was 78.4% with second-generation cash rents 15.7% lower in the third quarter, THE MART occupancy fell to 79.5%, and same-store cash NOI at the San Francisco office complex fell 42.5% over nine months on free rent. Street retail supplied 16.94% and the Other segment 14.54% of nine-month NOI at share, so the New York office portfolio carries the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is rising and most of the hedge book rolls off in 2027, so interest cover will not improve without EBITDA growth: the weighted average rate on consolidated debt rose to 4.91% from 4.73% at 2025-12-31, the weighted average rate on unsecured notes rose to 4.78% from 2.73% after 5.75% notes due 2033 replaced 2.15% notes, and 26.34% of principal floats. A one percentage point rise in base rates costs USD 11.48 million a year after current hedges, but the swaps and caps on the revolver, the term loan and five mortgage loans expire between February 2027 and October 2027, when the sensitivity will rise by an amount the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 79–81; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 128; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a squeeze in 2027 and 2028, when weaker office leasing or higher base rates would hit cash flow that already barely covers capital spending and preferred distributions just as USD 2,780.00 million of mortgages mature and the partnership begins funding about USD 290.00 million of cash to the Park Avenue development venture in mid-2028. An illustrative reversal of New York office occupancy to the 88.8% of 2024-12-31 would remove about USD 64.85 million of annual rent, lifting trailing leverage excluding gains to 9.15x and cutting cover to 2.47x with a one percentage point rise in base rates; liquidity, unused repurchase authority and asset sales would absorb it, so distress is not the base case. The signals to watch are look-through leverage, New York office occupancy and progress on refinancing the 2027 and 2028 mortgages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 73, 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an average view is asset value. The Park Avenue contribution was valued at USD 900.00 million against a USD 400.00 million loan and is expected to yield a net gain of about USD 485.00 million, the Alexander's stake has a market value of USD 407.73 million against a carrying amount of USD 84.27 million, book debt is 0.48x total assets, and the third-party units and common shares were worth about USD 6,895.62 million at the quarter-end price implied by the units' redemption value, which puts debt at 52.06% of debt plus equity at market value, an analyst proxy and not the covenant measure. Management also states that cash flow over the next twelve months together with cash balances will be adequate for its needs. Trailing leverage excluding gains falling below the FY2025 level of 7.74x through EBITDA growth rather than gains, mortgage refinancings at or below current size and asset sales that repay debt would move the view toward strong. New York office occupancy falling below the 91.2% of 2025-12-31, repurchases or joint-venture equity funded by revolver drawings while look-through leverage rises, recourse support for the Park Avenue venture's construction loan, or a share price fall that tightens the debt to market capitalization covenant would move it toward weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 28–29, 45, 70, 77; calculation CALC-21; calculation CALC-22; calculation CALC-23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The look-through ratios of 8.88x and 10.28x add debt of consolidated joint ventures at 100% to NOI after the minority share, so they overstate attributable leverage by a total the filings do not state; the 30% minority share of the USD 1,200.00 million San Francisco mortgage alone is USD 360.00 million and would lower the first ratio to 8.57x, which narrows but does not remove the finding that look-through leverage exceeds the consolidated ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2027 and 2028 mortgage amounts update the only printed ladder for documented 2026 refinancings and reconcile to mortgage principal, and the split of the 2027 amount between the satisfied USD 400.00 million loan and a USD 480.00 million remainder rests on loan sizes and a January 2027 maturity; an unreported prepayment or extension would lower the USD 2,780.00 million wall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, bond price or spread is supplied, so the view that capital-market access is adequate rests on one USD 500.00 million unsecured issue in January 2026 and cannot be tested against market pricing; a wide spread would move access to weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels and the definition of market capitalization are not printed, so the finding that liquidity and unsecured maturities are comfortable cannot be tested against covenant headroom, and the 52.06% debt to debt plus equity proxy drawn from the units' redemption value is not the covenant measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The unencumbered real estate of USD 4,155.48 million is the difference between book real estate and a pledged figure printed rounded to the nearest tenth of a billion, so the 1.83x cover of unsecured debt is approximate and rests on book rather than market values.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management guidance or forecast is supplied, so the outlook, the downside illustration and the monitoring signals are analyst judgement built from reported rent spreads, expirations, hedge dates and sensitivities, not management's plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit's strengths are an office franchise that is leasing at higher rents on rising occupancy, a tenant base with no tenant above 10% of revenues and ten largest tenants at 26.9% of rent, an unsecured maturity profile with nothing due before April 2029 if extensions are used, and asset values that appear to sit above book. Each links to cash flow or recovery: higher rents raise NOI, a diversified rent roll limits single-tenant loss, distant unsecured maturities remove a near-term refinancing event for the partnership's bank and note investors, and values above book support sales that repay debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 26–27, 45, 57–58; calculation CALC-21; calculation CALC-22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit's weaknesses are leverage above eight times on every gross-debt measure, free cash flow that is roughly zero after capital spending and preferred distributions and negative after the common distribution, a secured maturity wall in 2027 and 2028, floating-rate exposure with hedges expiring in 2027, and a large development whose financing, equity and anchor rent depend on one relationship. Each links to the capacity to deleverage: leverage cannot fall from internal cash, refinancing sets the pace, and an equity call beginning in mid-2028 competes with maturities in the same year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 70–73, 79–81; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine financial-profile dimensions the assessment is: scale and market position strong, with trailing revenues of USD 1,842.71 million and 26.50 million square feet in service at the partnership's share; competitive advantage average, strong in New York office and weaker in retail and non-New York assets; business diversification average, with tenant diversification strong and geographic and property-type concentration weak; cost and capex flexibility average; margin stability average; free cash flow stability weak; ability to refinance and access capital markets average; liquidity position strong over twelve months; and financial policy and governance average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 65, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 52; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vornado Realty L.P. is the operating partnership through which Vornado Realty Trust holds substantially all of its assets; the trust is sole general partner and owned about 91.2% of the common limited partnership interest at 2026-09-30. Creditor figures here use the partnership's own statements; the trust's per-share and funds-from-operations measures are context only. The business is a Manhattan-weighted office landlord with street retail, residential, THE MART in Chicago and a controlling interest in an office complex in San Francisco; the New York metropolitan area supplies 88% of NOI at share and office about 78% in FY2025. The Park Avenue development venture named in the findings is the venture on 350 Park Avenue formed on 2026-10-20, which is separate from the 49.0% interest in the Park Avenue Plaza office building bought in June 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rental revenues were 87.39% of nine-month revenues, from leases whose third-quarter New York office signings ran 9.5 years on average, so the revenue model is contractual rent with escalations and tenant reimbursements, plus smaller fee income from cleaning, management and leasing. That gives good cash-flow visibility and supports debt service, but the concentration in one market and one property type means a Manhattan office downturn would hit nearly all cash flow at once, and the partnership's ability to refinance depends on lenders' views of that market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 18, 50, 57, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trust is the sole general partner with exclusive control of day-to-day management, third-party Class A unitholders hold about 8.8% of common units with a right to tender for cash, and the trust has 48.79 million preferred shares outstanding whose distributions the partnership funds. Chairman and chief executive Steven Roth also leads Alexander's, and Interstate Properties and its partners held about 7.1% of the trust's shares and 26.0% of Alexander's at 2025-12-31, which the annual report calls substantial influence. For creditors the structure means the partnership's unsecured claims rank alongside other partnership-level liabilities but behind the creditors of operating subsidiaries and consolidated joint ventures, and cash leaves the partnership first to preferred distributions and then to the trust's common dividend; guarantors, a restricted group and the legal rank of each instrument are not established because the governing documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable and largely recurring but cyclical in its re-leasing. Leases are long (9.5 years on third-quarter New York office signings), expirations are spread (6.1%, 6.2% and 6.3% of New York office square feet in 2026, 2027 and 2028), and weighted average escalated office rent rose from USD 80.01 per square foot in 2021 to USD 90.56 in 2025 while occupancy moved between 88.8% and 92.2%. Pricing power is real in prime office, where second-generation rents rose 23.5% on a GAAP basis over nine months, and absent in retail, where cash rents fell 7.1%. The mechanism is that rolling 2026 expiring office rents of USD 79.82 per square foot to the USD 85 to 95 management expects on re-leasing raises NOI, while tenants' hybrid-work and space-reduction choices set the vacancy risk, so the credit implication is steady organic growth that must still outrun a higher interest bill.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating costs are largely fixed in the short run: mortgage payments, real estate taxes and maintenance do not fall when rents fall, the building-services workforce is unionised, and nine-month consolidated operating expenses rose 4.37% against revenue growth of 2.38%, taking the consolidated NOI margin to 48.47% from 49.45%. Same-store operations did better, with NOI at share up 8.4%, so the margin pressure came from acquisitions, development and non-reimbursable costs rather than the stabilised portfolio. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through reimbursements and escalations but not against a deep occupancy fall or a sharp rise in wage and energy costs, so operating leverage cuts both ways for interest cover. Multiemployer pension contributions of USD 9.65 million and health plan contributions of USD 34.88 million in FY2025 sit inside operating expenses, and withdrawal liability is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and part of it is discretionary. Leasing capital absorbs 13.1% of initial rent on New York office space signed in nine months, additions to real estate and development spending were USD 273.91 million in nine months, and non-cash rent adjustments of USD 116.34 million mean cash NOI at share was 86.72% of NOI at share. Growth capital can be deferred, but the remaining USD 195.73 million on the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment and the cash call from mid-2028 on the Park Avenue venture are commitments in practice. EBITDA therefore converts weakly into free cash flow: after cash interest, capital spending and preferred distributions the twelve-month figure is a shortfall of USD 10.74 million, so deleveraging has to come from asset sales or EBITDA growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 65–67, 70–73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters: the partnership competes with many owners and developers, some willing to accept lower returns, on rents, concessions, location and building quality, and tenants have moved to modern amenitised buildings; the mechanism is higher concessions and capital to hold Class A status, and the implication is that leasing capital stays near 12% to 13% of initial rent. New entrants take the form of newer, more amenitised competing buildings in the same market, which the annual report names as a risk to leasing and effective rents, and the threat of substitutes is real through hybrid work, co-working, sublease space and artificial-intelligence-driven space reduction, which could cut demand for office space in the largest tenant industries, financial services at 23% and technology at 13% of rents. Buyer power is moderate: no tenant exceeds 10% of revenues and the ten largest are 26.9% of rent, but large tenants negotiate free rent and allowances. Supplier power is moderate: building-services labour is unionised and construction and renovation costs are named as a factor in results, and the annual report says it is not assured that increases in operating costs can be passed through to tenants in full.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors matter through three channels only. Economic: base rates and refinancing conditions set interest cost on the USD 1,972.54 million of floating-rate consolidated debt, and New York employment and tourism set rents. Political and regulatory: New York City's Local Law 97 carbon limits, the State's grid decarbonisation mandate and the gas-ban bill could raise operating and retrofit costs and decrease cash available for obligations, though the annual report states no material effect to date. Social and technological: hybrid work and artificial-intelligence-driven space use set long-run demand for office space. Other political and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths in credit terms: leasing momentum and rising occupancy in New York office; ten largest tenants at 26.9% of rent with no tenant above 10% of revenues; unsecured maturities beyond April 2029; liquidity of USD 1,768.78 million; asset values above book. Weaknesses: leverage of 8.08x trailing EBITDA and 8.88x look-through NOI at share; free cash flow near zero; secured maturities of USD 2,780.00 million in 2027 and 2028; concentration in one market and property type. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: sales or joint-venture monetisations at values above book that repay debt, and delivery of the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment in 2027. Threats that could weaken it: a sharp rise in vacancy, refinancing at higher coupons as hedges expire in 2027, joint-venture equity calls and recourse support for the Park Avenue venture's construction loan, and a lower share price tightening a market-based covenant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 26–27, 45, 57–58, 73, 79–81; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 51; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weaker than the business profile. Consolidated debt of USD 7,448.31 million is 0.48x total assets at book, but EBITDA derived by Financial foundation covers cash interest only 2.89x and trailing leverage excluding gains of 8.47x is above the FY2025 underlying 7.74x. Trend is mixed: underlying leverage improved in 2025 and has risen again in 2026 as borrowings funded joint-venture investments, acquisitions and repurchases, while look-through leverage on NOI at share rose from 8.72x to 8.88x. Main supports are liquidity, distant unsecured maturities and asset values; main constraints are leverage, near-zero free cash flow and the secured wall; key missing datapoints are covenant levels, ratings, the minority share of consolidated joint-venture debt and a ladder at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt stack at 2026-09-30 is USD 4,869.54 million of mortgages (USD 3,340.00 million fixed at a weighted 4.98% and USD 1,529.54 million floating at 5.65%), USD 850.00 million of senior unsecured notes (USD 350.00 million due 2031 and USD 500.00 million due 2033), an USD 850.00 million term loan to February 2031 and USD 918.00 million drawn on two revolvers with USD 2,130.00 million of commitments; carrying value is USD 39.23 million below principal after financing costs. Claims outside the debt figure are lease liabilities of USD 694.36 million on ground leases with a weighted remaining term of 46.7 years (undiscounted payments of USD 2,001.61 million at 2025-12-31, of which USD 45.06 million fell due in 2026), USD 508.98 million of future rent and fixed payments in lieu of taxes on the Farley Building lease, which is accounted for as a failed sale-leaseback and excluded from those lease liabilities, redeemable third-party Class A units of USD 561.48 million with a cash redemption right, a redeemable interest of USD 68.16 million held by the Farley Building tax credit investor, guarantees of about USD 193.36 million, letters of credit of USD 23.72 million drawn on the revolvers and construction commitments of USD 11.93 million; participation in multiemployer pension plans is stated as not significant. No filing describes factoring, supplier finance or consent-decree funding, and retiree health benefits are provided only through multiemployer health plans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27, 29, 42–43, 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 147–150; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are lease-up and rent growth in New York office (the Fifth Avenue office redevelopment is due for delivery in 2027), a lower development outlay once it completes, and a consolidated debt stack with no unsecured maturity before April 2029; the headwinds are the end of the Seventh Avenue waiver of default interest in March 2027, USD 480.00 million of mortgages due in 2027 and USD 2,300.00 million in 2028, expiry of swaps and caps between February 2027 and October 2027, and a distribution of about USD 153.30 million in the fourth quarter if the 2025 rate is repeated. Over 3 to 5 years the equity call of about USD 290.00 million from mid-2028 on a USD 6,250.00 million development, drawing of its USD 3,300.00 million construction loan (about USD 1,191.30 million at the partnership's 36.1% effective share if fully drawn, an analyst inference), and the preferred equity return on the Fifth Avenue and Times Square joint venture moving from 4.75% to a formula after April 2029 are the main swing factors. The sector tailwind is tenants' preference for high-quality, modern, well-located buildings, which favours the partnership's Class A office; sector headwinds are hybrid work, tenant space reduction and retail weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 26, 45, 73, 79–81; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 128–129; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a Manhattan office leasing slowdown, with tenants cutting space under hybrid work and artificial-intelligence-driven reductions while base rates stay high. The first operating break is lower occupancy: a return of New York office occupancy to the 88.8% of 2024-12-31, 4.2 percentage points below 93.0%, would vacate about 716,142 square feet of the partnership's share at USD 90.56 of annual escalated rent, or USD 64.85 million of rent, 7.38% of trailing EBITDA excluding gains, assuming no expense savings and no re-letting. The financial transmission is EBITDA of USD 814.19 million, total debt over EBITDA of 9.15x and, with a one percentage point rise in base rates costing USD 11.48 million, cash interest of USD 330.28 million and cover of 2.47x. The liquidity and refinancing consequence is that USD 2,780.00 million of mortgages and the USD 244.54 million Seventh Avenue loan must be refinanced into weaker property income, while the equity call begins in mid-2028; USD 1,188.28 million of undrawn revolver capacity, no unsecured maturity before April 2029, USD 286.59 million of repurchase authority the board need not use, deferral of the remaining Fifth Avenue office spend, asset sales and the non-recourse nature of property loans other than guarantees of about USD 193.36 million are the levers. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event over 24 months, but the equity cushion would thin, and the observable triggers are occupancy below 91.2%, negative second-generation rent spreads, revolver drawings above USD 918.00 million and no refinancing progress six months before a maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 42, 57–58, 70, 73, 77, 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_vno-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation CALC-20; calculation CALC-24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked drivers are in the materiality register in the appendix: six negatives led by look-through leverage and the 2027 to 2028 mortgage wall, and three positives, liquidity with distant unsecured maturities, New York office leasing momentum and asset values above book. The two that decide the view are whether EBITDA grows faster than debt and whether the secured wall is refinanced without paydown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is strong because leases are long and tenants diversified, with the downside path through office vacancy and rent resets. Margin resilience is average, with the path through operating costs that do not fall with rents. Free cash flow conversion is weak, with the path through capital spending and distributions exceeding operating cash flow. Liquidity buffer is strong over twelve months, with the path through a mortgage-market shock that forces revolver use. Refinancing capacity is average, resting on one unsecured issue in January 2026 and the secured wall, with the path through higher coupons. Governance and financial policy is average, with the path through buybacks and joint-venture equity while leverage is high. Primary downside path: weaker office income meeting the 2027 and 2028 mortgage maturities and the mid-2028 equity call with cash flow that is already near zero after capital spending and distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vno-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58, 70, 73; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The triggers are in the register in the appendix. Where no covenant or documented threshold exists, each signal uses the partnership's own reported levels as the reference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Vornado Realty L.P. presents a strong business profile supported by a leasing-led Manhattan office franchise at 93.0% occupancy, a tenant base with none above 10% of revenues and liquidity of USD 1,768.78 million, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 8.08x trailing EBITDA and 8.88x look-through NOI at share and by free cash flow that is near zero after capital spending and preferred distributions. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because rents are contractual and rising, but not strong because cash conversion lags and discretionary spending runs ahead of deleveraging. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on lenders' appetite for Manhattan office mortgages in 2027 and 2028, on hedge costs, and on the partnership's willingness to pause repurchases and sell assets. The primary downside path is weaker office income meeting the secured maturity wall and the mid-2028 equity call. Further analysis would require covenant levels and agreements, agency ratings and market pricing, the minority share of consolidated joint-venture debt, the Park Avenue venture's agreement and a ladder at 2026-09-30. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: a 2027 to 2028 refinancing squeeze on already high leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amounts are in USD million unless stated; statement figures printed in thousands are divided by 1,000 and rounded to two decimals for the findings, with the unrounded figure kept in the inputs.

fields.value: - The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is not printed. The ladder used here updates the ladder at 2025-12-31 for the documented 2026 refinancings and reconciles to mortgage principal of USD 4,869.54 million, but an unreported prepayment or extension would change the 2027 and 2028 amounts; this is a medium-severity gap that a ladder at 2026-09-30 would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels are not printed anywhere, compliance with the financial covenants is stated only as at 2025-12-31, and the definition of market capitalization is not given, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the annual report names total debt to total assets, secured debt to total assets, EBITDA to interest expense, fixed charges and unencumbered assets to unsecured debt as covenant families, and the agreements' own EBITDA and interest definitions differ from the derived EBITDA over cash interest paid used here; this is a medium-severity gap that the credit agreements and indentures would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, outlook, bond price or spread is supplied, so market access is judged from one unsecured issue in January 2026 only; this is a medium-severity gap that rating reports and dated quotes would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The total minority share of consolidated joint-venture debt is not stated, so look-through debt attributable to the partnership cannot be computed and the figures of 8.88x and 10.28x overstate it by an unknown amount, of which USD 360.00 million is the minority share of the San Francisco mortgage; this is a medium-severity gap that a schedule of consolidated joint-venture debt by owner would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The market-risk table totals the pro rata share of non-consolidated debt but gives no maturities, so the refinancing profile of USD 2,732.55 million of joint-venture debt is not established; this is a medium-severity gap that a joint-venture debt schedule would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The construction loan of the Park Avenue development venture, USD 3,300.00 million, has no stated guarantee or recourse terms and is not yet part of pro rata debt; if fully drawn it would add about USD 1,191.30 million at the partnership's effective share, an analyst inference; this is a medium-severity gap that the venture agreement would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set is supplied, so the judgement that leverage near eight times is high rests on the partnership's own history and general credit norms rather than a comparison with other office landlords; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management gives no guidance and no forecast is supplied, so the outlook and downside illustration are analyst judgement; the downside illustration assumes no expense savings and no re-letting; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma net debt after the 2026-10-20 joint venture closing is not established because the filing gives no cash effect; this is a low-severity gap that the next quarterly report would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outcome of the PENN 1 ground rent arbitration and litigation is uncertain, with annual rent of USD 15.00 million being paid against a possible USD 20.22 million retroactive to June 2023; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing or release after the third-quarter report signed on 2026-11-02 is supplied, so events in the sixteen days to the as-of date are not covered; this is a low-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
